title: Chronic Dexamethasone Disturbs the Circadian Rhythm of Melatonin and Clock Genes Causing Intestinal Barrier Damage in Goats
content: Dex is a common hormone drug commonly used as an immunosuppressive and anti-inflammatory agent in humans and animals. GCs have profound impact on melatonin expression and biological rhythm. However, the effect of chronic expose to Dex on melatonin secretion and biological clock gene expression in ruminants is still unclear. Ten sheep were randomly divided into two groups: the control group were injected with saline, and the Dex-treated group were intramuscularly injected daily for 21 d with 0.2 mg/kg Dex. The results showed that the rhythm of melatonin secretion in the plasma changes, and the plasma and colon levels of melatonin were lower in the Dex group compared to the control group (P&lt;0.05). Dex leads to a significant decrease in the expression of Arylalkylamine N-acetyltransferase (AANAT), a key melatonin synthase, in the pineal gland and colon. Detecting intestinal leakage-related indexes showed that diamine oxidase (DAO) and lipopolysaccharide (LPS) content increased significantly in the Dex group (P&lt;0.05). We also detected genes associated with biological rhythms in plasma. The results showed that in control group, the five tested genes showed circadian rhythms, but the circadian rhythms of Clock, Cry1, Cry2 and Per2 were abolished or blunted by the Dex (P&lt;0.05). Protein levels of CLOCK and BMAL1 in the colon changed significantly (P&lt;0.05). In conclusion, the above experimental results show that chronic exposure to Dex leads to the disorder of circadian rhythms of melatonin secretion and clock genes and may impaired intestinal barrier function.
